around.headline: Bengaluru techie found dead with husband after fight over house ownership; police say he suffocated her then died by suicide
around.summary: A techie was found dead alongside her husband at their home in Rajagopalnagar, with police saying an argument over who owned the house ended in him suffocating her before he died by suicide. If a dispute over property or money in your own home is escalating in intensity, involve family elders, a lawyer, or the police early — don't wait for it to reach a breaking point.
around.source: NDTV, The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: Bengaluru traffic turns brutal again: commuters abandon cars and autos, walk the last stretch home
around.summary: A startup founder took 90 minutes to cover just 3km before giving up and walking, and separately another commuter got off his auto to walk 2km home, as Saturday evening traffic snarled across the city. If you're heading out tonight, check live traffic before you leave and keep a walkable backup plan for the last mile.
around.source: NDTV, The Economic Times, Hindustan Times, Moneycontrol

around.headline: Metro's Yellow Line gets a 15th train as BMRCL eyes 6-minute peak-hour frequency
around.summary: Bengaluru Metro inducted a 15th train on the Yellow Line, part of a push to bring peak-hour frequency down to 6 minutes. Worth checking if your commute route touches the Yellow Line — waits should shorten as more trains join service.

around.headline: In first I-Day address as CM, Shivakumar announces Bengaluru police split into five commissionerates, plus a Jobs Mission and AI university
around.summary: CM DK Shivakumar used his Independence Day speech to formalise splitting Bengaluru's police commissionerate into five units for law and order, and separately announced a new 'Jobs Mission', an AI university and tech hubs beyond Bengaluru city; four police personnel were meanwhile suspended for leaking confidential details about the new commissionerate structure ahead of time.
around.source: The Hindu, The Indian Express, Moneycontrol, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Footpaths Bengaluru cleared of encroachments are filling back up, raising pedestrian-safety questions
around.summary: Footpaths that were cleared of encroachments in earlier civic drives are seeing hawkers and parked vehicles creep back, according to a fresh on-ground check across the city. If your daily walk includes a stretch like this, factor in extra caution — and report repeat encroachments to your ward's BBMP helpline.

around.headline: 7.7-magnitude earthquake in Indonesia kills at least 38, flattens buildings
around.summary: A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck Indonesia, killing at least 38 people and collapsing buildings, with visuals showing residents fleeing. If you have friends or family in the region, it's worth checking in — and a good reminder to know your own building's basic earthquake safety steps, since parts of Karnataka sit in a low-but-nonzero seismic zone.

street_smart.title: You took a small 'instant loan' from an app for an emergency, paid back a couple of days late, and now you're getting nonstop calls threatening to send a morphed, embarrassing photo of you to everyone in your phone contacts unless you pay a huge 'penalty' right now. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: No single Bengaluru incident in today's feeds fit the choice-based format cleanly (today's biggest safety story is a murder-suicide, which doesn't lend itself to a 'best move' quiz). Rotating in from the evergreen list instead: loan-app harassment. A similar scenario last ran on 2026-07-24, just outside the 3-week window, and every other evergreen topic (digital arrest, UPI fraud, auto overcharging, rental traps, job scams, OTP scams, two-wheeler theft, medical emergencies, tenant/landlord rights, consumer court, phone snatching, card skimming) has appeared more recently.
street_smart.situation: The app you borrowed ₹5,000 from now claims you owe over ₹50,000 in 'penalties' and 'processing fees' that were never disclosed upfront, and the harassment has already started reaching your family group chats.

choices.text: Pay the inflated penalty immediately via UPI so the calls and messages stop.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Paying confirms you'll cave under pressure, and victims typically report the demands escalate rather than stop — legitimate lenders can't legally threaten your contacts or morph your photos; that's already a crime, not a debt-recovery tactic.

choices.text: Block the number, delete the app, and stay quiet about it, hoping it blows over.
choices.feedback: Risky. Blocking one number rarely helps since these operations call from many numbers and keep contacting your family directly — staying silent also means your contacts see the threatening messages with no context, which is exactly what makes the shame tactic work.

choices.text: Screenshot every threatening call and message, report the app to the National Cyber Crime portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or call 1930, and give your close contacts a heads-up that it's a scam before the harassment reaches them.
choices.feedback: Correct. Contacting your personal contacts and sending morphed images is illegal harassment, not legitimate recovery — documenting evidence and reporting to cybercrime.gov.in or 1930 gets the app flagged for takedown, and warning your contacts ahead of time strips the tactic of its power.

choices.text: Take out a loan from a second app to pay off the first one's 'penalty'.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. It only compounds the problem — you'd now owe two predatory lenders instead of one, and the second app is just as likely to run the same contact-harassment playbook once a payment is late.

takeaways: A lender contacting your personal contacts or threatening to share your photos is illegal harassment — not a legitimate debt-recovery method, no matter what the app's terms say.
Only borrow from RBI-registered NBFCs or their listed partner apps; check the lender's name against the RBI's list before installing anything that asks for contact-list access.
Report harassment immediately to the National Cyber Crime helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in — documented evidence (screenshots, call logs) makes takedown and any recovery action faster.

quiz.question: A Bengaluru startup founder went viral today after how long it took him to cover just 3km through traffic before giving up and walking home?
quiz.why: He wasn't alone — another commuter separately got off his auto the same evening and walked 2km home rather than sit in the same jam.

quiz.question: In his first Independence Day address as CM, DK Shivakumar announced Bengaluru's police commissionerate will be split into how many units?
quiz.why: The same speech also announced a new 'Jobs Mission' and an AI university as part of a 'Beyond Bengaluru' push to spread tech growth across Karnataka.

quiz.question: A powerful earthquake struck Indonesia today, killing at least 38 people and collapsing buildings. What was its magnitude?
quiz.why: Indonesia sits on the seismically active 'Ring of Fire', which is why the country experiences frequent large earthquakes and volcanic activity.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's piped drinking water is drawn mainly from which river, despite its basin lying over 100km from the city?
quiz.why: The Cauvery is also at the centre of a long-running interstate water-sharing dispute with Tamil Nadu, which is back in the news today over water releases from the KRS dam.

quiz.question: The Karnataka High Court is housed in which landmark Bengaluru building, located next to Vidhana Soudha?
quiz.why: 'Attara Kacheri' means '18 offices' in Urdu/Kannada, a nod to the departments once housed there during British rule before it became the High Court.
